verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced it by running the real notifier, and it does what the reviewer says.

Code: at scripts/notify-transfers.mjs:119-121, decide() has only two outcomes once d.worth is true. If confidenceLevel(why.confidence) is 'CONFIDENT' the head is '🎯 забирай'. Anything else gets '🤔 Тебе: можно взять X, но не уверенно'. Nothing checks DOUBTFUL. acquisition().worth looks only at the season edge (at least 15 FP), not at confidence, so 52-59% deals reach the 🤔 branch.

The branch's own stated rules disagree with this:
- src/season.js:560 says "below DOUBTFUL it is not worth a transfer".
- returnHead() in scripts/telegram-format.mjs is new in this branch. It sends nothing below 60%, and its comment says "the same bars as the other advice". tests/season-ui.test.js:114 asserts returnHead(.56) is null.
- The comment at notify-transfers.mjs:46 and pickPackage() drop doubtful packages ("a doubtful one is not shown").
- The app shows DOUBTFUL as the 'не стоит' chip (season-ui.js:141).
- The season-transfers group's own note to season-ui said "skip below 60%" for the Telegram alerts, but decide() only got the confidenceLevel/`when` change, not that gate.

So the same 54% deal reads "можно взять" in the rival-transfer message and "не стоит" in the app. A return alert at that confidence would not be sent at all.

Not a regression: on origin/main decide() also had two branches (confidence>=CONFIDENT → 🎯, else 🤔). The inconsistency comes from the branch adding the 60% gate to returns and packages but not here.

Possible refutation, which I don't think holds: ACCEPTANCE.md:168 (historical 19.10 entry) says "'забирай' in Telegram needs 70%, otherwise the bot offers the move as not sure", and the collapsed details do print "сомнительно". But the same line says "Moves are advised from 70%; below 60% they are marked doubtful". The head is an offer ("можно взять") and shows no percentage, and the code contracts above define below-60% as not worth a transfer. No owner decision makes below-60% deals buy offers. "Advice maximises expected points" is about the objective; every other channel still applies the confidence gate.

How often it happens: I scanned the live 21.10 data for team 0 (bank 200, 3 transfers left). Of 21 rival-held players whose release would be 'worth' a move, 6 are DOUBTFUL: Banchero 59, Giddey 54, MPJ 54, Kawhi 59, Boozer 59, Trey Murphy 52. Each would get the 🤔 offer. This matches the reviewer's list exactly.

Severity: medium. The head is hedged and the details show the percent and "сомнительно". But it contradicts the app and the other Telegram channels for about a quarter of the worth-flagged releases. The left=0 'spent' branch also prints the next-week deal for doubtful cases; that is the same issue in milder form.

findings.title: After the projection-inputs merge, playRate drops ESPN's half of the forecast for Out players with a dated return
findings.location: src/season.js:152-154 (playRate prior), against scripts/projection_model.py:735-772 (apply: games, knownAbsence, availability.unconditionalGames)
findings.claim: apply() now writes forecast.games for a player with a known absence as the post-return mean (model_post+min(ESPN,left))/2. For a blocked player F<U is the normal case, so the prior becomes U/82. injuryFactor removes the blocked games, and the Season tab then expects left*U/82 games. That is the model-only post-return figure: owner decision 4 (mean of ESPN and model) is lost, and the Season tab disagrees with the forecast card. The merge turned the shipped max(F,U) into the 'U alone' variant that the season-availability group measured and rejected (Strus 60.7->30.5, Beal 49.1->31.2, Porzingis 45.4->31.6). JS reads forecast.knownAbsence nowhere.

verdict.reasoning:
I confirmed the defect from the code and on realistic data. The mechanism is wider than the finding says.

What the code does:
- scripts/projection_model.py apply() (merged, commit 967f2c6) handles a dated Out/Suspension block as follows:
  - left = 82 - blocked
  - model_games = healthy_mean(U*left/82, left), which includes the healthy-start uplift
  - espn_games = min(E, left)
  - forecast.games = (model_games + espn_games)/2, which covers only the post-return games
  - It writes knownAbsence {blockedGames, gamesLeft, ...} and availability.unconditionalGames = U (report-free, over 82 games).
- src/season.js playRate (lines 152-154) for an Out report sets prior = clamp(max(F, U)/82). Then injuryFactor zeroes every game before the return. The Season tab's post-return expectation is therefore about (games after return) * max(F, U)/82, plus a little chain front-loading.
- Nothing in src/ reads forecast.knownAbsence; only forecast-text.js reads gamesBasis. projection-inputs' REQUIRED crossGroupNotes item (prior = f.games/knownAbsence.gamesLeft) was never applied in the merge.

There are two failure modes. The finding names only the first:
- (a) F < U: the prior is U/82. ESPN's half (owner decision 4) and the post-return healthy-start uplift are lost. The result can go either way: Moody is overstated, Butler, Sharpe and Penda are understated.
- (b) F >= U, common for ESPN-combined players (Porzingis, Strus, Beal, Claxton, Nurkic, Harris, Stewart, Vukcevic, Gueye): the prior is F/82. F already excludes the blocked games, and injuryFactor removes them again, so the block is counted twice. This is exactly projection-inputs' risk 1.

So the finding's wording "U alone" is too narrow, but the defect is real: in every case the Season tab disagrees with the forecast card. The same share feeds:
- playerPicture and expectedPoints, which drive transfer advice, injuredTargets and bestTransfers
- the rate() in season.js:464

Reachability: the deployed public/data has no knownAbsence yet. The effect appears with the first CI build that runs the merged projection_model.py (34 players carry knownAbsence in the projection-inputs rebuild). The test 'an ESPN total that priced the reported absence…' passes only because its fixture has the pre-merge shape: no knownAbsence and F = ESPN's full-season total.

Caveat: my real-data run uses the projection-inputs harness DB (scratchpad/pi/after-schedule.json), built by that branch's apply() before the projection-model merge (HEALTHY_SHIFT refit). Absolute numbers will shift slightly after a real rebuild. The structural mismatch is independent of that.

findings.title: The capped injury spell expires at the return, so a returning player's share collapses the day he plays
findings.location: src/season.js:158-161 (cap only while keptOut and only on the trailing run); scripts/inseason_calibration.py availability()/return_cases (fitted only at the instant before the first game back)
findings.claim: While ESPN lists the player Out, the current run of misses counts as at most spellMisses=4. Once he plays (or ESPN drops the report), every missed game counts again. The Python fit (holdout.availabilityAtReturn) measures the cap at the moment just before the first game back, while the run is still trailing. One game later the app is back on the uncapped estimator, whose return bias the calibration JSON itself reports as -0.135 share. So the value is high during the absence and drops by about 40% at the return. That is exactly when 'вернулся в строй' / injuredTargets advice is generated.
findings.reproduction: Scratch file review2/season/ret.mjs. A player with forecast games 70 who played 10 club games and missed 30. While Out (return = next game's US day): playRate .796, rest of season 33.4 games / 1021 FP. Next day, after his first game back with the report removed: playRate .460, 18.9 games / 575 FP.
findings.fix: Cap the most recent completed spell of 10 or more misses (for example until N games after the return, or, with injury-history, every run that overlaps a reported Out episode), not only a trailing run while the report lasts. Re-fit in inseason_calibration.py at checkpoints after the return (t+1..t+10), not only at t.

verdict.reasoning:
The code does what the finding says. In src/season.js playRate (lines 155-169), the spell cap is applied only when `out` is true, which means keptOut(injury) && !seasonEnding. It only shortens the trailing run of misses after the last played game. Two things switch it off:
(1) He plays his first game back. The trailing run is then 0, and every missed game counts again in `team`.
(2) ESPN drops the report or downgrades it to Day-To-Day / GTD. Then keptOut is false. This can happen before he has played at all.
Both also remove the `max(f.games, free)` lift of the prior.

The repo's own data says the uncapped estimator runs low just after a return. I re-ran inseason_calibration.py's own functions (team_sequences, availability) on data/raw 2023-26. The checkpoints were t+d after the first game back from a 10+ miss spell, and from d>=1 the app uses the uncapped value. Bias of the uncapped value:
- holdout 2024/25->2025/26: -0.102 at d=1, -0.099 at d=3, -0.087 at d=5, -0.050 at d=10 (n about 110-120)
- fit pair: -0.149, -0.129, -0.120, -0.073

So for about 5-10 games after the return, the share is low by about 0.1, which is several games and roughly 100+ FP over the rest of the season. While Out, the same player had been valued at the capped, roughly unbiased level (+0.04).

This matters for advice. injuredTargets values report-carrying players at the capped rate, and says the 4-week window "is checked again once he is back". At that point the rate has collapsed, so the advice flips for exactly the players it recommended.

The scoping is mentioned in the JSON limitations ("in the app it applies while an injury report keeps the player out"). But that is a statement of scope, not an owner decision. The code comment's reason (do not count the absence twice while injuryFactor removes the games) says nothing about the period after the return. And the calibration evidence shows the absence still misleads the estimate after it.

How big it is: the synthetic 30-miss case shows a drop of about 42%. Real backtest cases show about 0.1 share of bias. The bias before the return is not new (main never capped). The new part is the discontinuity and the advice flip, which come from the cap applying only while Out.

My own scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Nba-draft-simulator/bb5a3e80-4ef5-52c7-bdfc-4c0abaeb739b/scratchpad/review2/skeptic-ret/. Run them from review-wt.

- B: same day, ESPN shows Day-To-Day/GTD instead: share 0.451, 18.5 games / 565 FP (collapses before he plays)
- C: played game 40, report removed: share 0.460, 18.9 games / 575 FP
- D: played games 40-44: share 0.493, 18.3 games / 555 FP

So C equals E: once he is back, the spell counts in full.

2) after.py on data/raw, uncapped availability() at t+d after the first game back from a 10+ miss spell (the app's value for d>=1):
- holdout: bias -0.135 (d=0), -0.102 (d=1), -0.099 (d=3), -0.087 (d=5); MAE 0.276 at d=1

verdict.fix:
Keep the cap on the most recent spell after the player returns, not only while the trailing run lasts under an Out report.

In playRate:
- Find the most recent run of >= spellGames (10) consecutive missed club games: finished club dates with no played row, between played games or trailing.
- Trailing run under a keptOut report: cap it at spellMisses (4), as now.
- The same trailing run under a Day-To-Day/GTD report should be capped the same way.
- Once the run is completed (he has played since), subtract run - min(run, spellMissesAfterReturn) from `team` for as long as it is the latest such spell. No report is needed for this, because the backtest measured it without reports.

findings.title: From 00:00 MSK on game night, a GTD report halves three games instead of one
findings.location: src/season.js:222 (injuryFactor: back>=today compares an ESPN US day with the Moscow date)
findings.claim: For a day-to-day player, ESPN's returnDate is the US day of the doubtful game. From midnight Moscow time the Moscow date is one day ahead of the US day (until about 08:00 MSK, and longer if ESPN has not updated the report yet). The return date then looks stale, and the fallback gives 0.5 to every game of the next three days. This happens during the live-game hours the user wants to follow, and it moves the week forecast and standings for about 50 GTD players every night.
findings.reproduction: Scratch file review2/season/gtd.mjs. Calendar: Moscow 22.10, 24.10, 25.10, 27.10. Report {Day-To-Day, GTD, returnDate 2026-10-21}. At 23:00 MSK on 21.10 the factors are .5,1,1,1 (week games 3.39). At 03:00 MSK on 22.10, with the same report, they are .5,.5,.5,1 (2.42).
findings.fix: Compare the return date with the current US day (for example usDay of now, or addDays(today,-1)), or pass ctx.now and derive the US day from it.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this. The day-to-day branch of injuryFactor in src/season.js (lines 217-221 at 967f2c6) is:
`return day<=(back&&back>=today?back:addDays(today,2))?.5:1;`
Here `back` is ESPN's returnDate, which is a US day. `day` is usDay(g), the game's US day, computed as tip minus 5 h. `today` is ctx.today, which both season-ui context() and notify-transfers set to moscowToday(), the Moscow date. The comment above the function says the same: "today is the Moscow date".

So `back>=today` compares a US day with a Moscow date. From 00:00 MSK the Moscow date is one day ahead of the US day. ESPN's return date for tonight's doubtful game then fails the test, and the code uses the fallback meant for stale reports: every game up to US day today+2 gets 0.5. That contradicts the function's own rule ("the games up to it count half ... with one already past, those of the next 3 days do"). The date is not past in US time.

The deployed report bears this out. ESPN's GTD returnDate is the US day of the club's next game: 47 GTD players carry 2026-10-21, the US night game that Sports.ru files under Moscow 22.10. The window lasts from 00:00 MSK until the US day turns over, at 08:00 MSK on the UTC-5 convention that usDay uses. That covers the live-game hours, and the UI recomputes context() during them through the live refresh from #89. The notifier also builds its ctx with moscowToday() whenever it runs.

Is it intended? No. The season-availability group listed it only as a known limitation (risk 4, "GTD at night"). No owner decision or doc makes it intended, and the existing tests use only daytime dates, so they pass.

Why medium: the weekly forecast of about 50 GTD players drops roughly 40% for about 8 hours every night. That moves the week totals and the standings odds shown at night. Transfers cannot be made in that window (08:00-22:00 only), and from 08:00 the result equals the intended stale-report behaviour, so advice acted on in the window is barely affected.
verdict.reproduction:

- 2026-10-21T20:59Z (23:59 MSK, today 21.10): 0.5, 1, 1, 1
- 2026-10-21T21:00Z (00:00 MSK, today 22.10, US day still 21.10): 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5
- 2026-10-22T04:59Z: the same
The flip happens exactly at Moscow midnight.

2) Real deployed data. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Nba-draft-simulator/bb5a3e80-4ef5-52c7-bdfc-4c0abaeb739b/scratchpad/review2/gtd-skeptic/real.mjs. It uses public/data/sports-current.json (espnInjuries via parseInjuries), default-draft.json players, and horizons(ctx).week. It finds 47 GTD players with returnDate 2026-10-21. Grayson Allen (Charlotte; Moscow games 22, 24, 25, 27.10, which are US days 21, 23, 24, 26.10):
- at 23:00 MSK on 21.10: factors 0.5, 1, 1, 1; week games 2.22
- at 03:00 and 07:30 MSK on 22.10, same report: factors 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1; week games 1.34
Knueppel goes 2.38 -> 1.43, Coby White 2.35 -> 1.42, Zach Collins (Chicago) 2.07 -> 1.25.

3) node --test tests/season-availability.test.js passes. Its GTD cases use only daytime pairs (today 2026-10-20 or 2026-10-21 with back 2026-10-21), so the night case is not covered.
verdict.fix:
Judge whether the report is stale against the current US day, not the Moscow date.

In src/season.js:
`export function injuryFactor(injury,day,today,usToday=today){ ... return day<=(back&&back>=usToday?back:addDays(usToday,2))?.5:1; }`

In expectedPoints, call `injuryFactor(injury,usDay(g),ctx.today,usNowOf(ctx))`, where:
`const usNowOf=ctx=>{const t=ctx.now??(ctx.today===moscowToday()?Date.now():null);return t==null?ctx.today:new Date(t-5*3600e3).toISOString().slice(0,10);}`
This uses the same UTC-5 convention as usDay. An alternative is to have season-ui context() and notify-transfers set ctx.usToday the same way.

Do not use addDays(today,-1). In daytime it would treat a report that is one day stale as fresh, and give 1 to every remaining game instead of the documented 3-day fallback.

Add a test: the same GTD report at 03:00 MSK on 22.10 should give 0.5 for US 21.10 and 1 for US 23.10.

findings.title: The live forecast drops by a whole game's expectation as soon as a player checks in
findings.location: src/season.js:248 (ahead excludes g.date===running); src/standings.js:47 and src/season-ui.js:270 add only running points
findings.claim: Once a player has an ESPN box line, expectedPoints drops that game from the rest-of-season expectation. The race and the Teams tab add only the points scored so far. Mid-game the forecast total, place and P(1st)/P(top-3) are therefore too low by about (1 - fraction played) x the game's expectation for every player on the floor. With the 20-second refresh (#89) these numbers dip at each tip-off and climb back by the final whistle. The behaviour is pre-existing (#87) but central to live tracking.
findings.reproduction: Scratch file review2/season/dip.mjs. A 40-FP/game player with three week games. Before tip-off the week forecast is 116.4. In the first quarter, with running {points:2, day:'2026-10-22'}, it is 2 + 77.6 = 79.6.
findings.fix: For a running game, count max(running points, expected game value x share), or running points plus the expected remainder scaled by the minutes left. Do not drop the game's expectation entirely.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced the dip myself. In src/season.js:248 expectedPoints removes a game from `ahead` once `g.date===running`, which is ctx.running.get(id).day. ctx.running comes from livePoints() (season-ui.js:122). That function adds an entry as soon as ESPN's box score has a stats line for the player. Starters get one at tip-off, already worth +1 from the participation bonus. leagueRace (standings.js:46-50) sets total = official + now + rest, with now = running points so far and rest = playerOutlook(...).season without that game. placeProbabilities then draws around this total. On the Teams tab, ahead() (season-ui.js:270) and teamKpis (season-ui.js:406) do the same. So the part of the game still to be played is not counted anywhere. Mid-game, every forecast for a player on the floor is about (1 - fraction played) x the game's value too low, and it comes back only at the final whistle.

Is it intended? Not as such. ACCEPTANCE.md:136 and the test at season.test.js:235 ("a running or already listed game is not expected again") come from #38. Their stated aim is to stop counting live points twice. Neither the docs nor the commit say the rest of a running game is worth nothing. No owner decision covers it. The dropping rule itself is old (#38). The P(1st)/P(top-3) chances that now read the lowered total are new on this branch.

The magnitude is real and visible:
- The 'Прогноз' column of the standings drops by about 16-40 FP per player on the floor.
- The Teams-tab forecast for the week drops by the same amount.
- P(1st) moves by 1-2 points early in the season. Late in the season, when the spread of the rest is small, it moves by tens of points.

Mitigating points: the error lasts only while games run and is gone at the final whistle. Transfer gains are not affected, because a move cannot gain a game in progress, so dropping it there is right. That keeps it at medium, not critical.
verdict.reproduction:
1) node review2/season/dip.mjs (the reviewer's file), run against review-wt. Before tip-off the week forecast is 116.4. With running {points:2, day:'2026-10-22'} the rest is 77.6, so the shown total is 79.6. That is a drop of 36.8 for a 40-FP/game player.
2) My file /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Nba-draft-simulator/bb5a3e80-4ef5-52c7-bdfc-4c0abaeb739b/scratchpad/review2/skeptic-dip/race.mjs uses the 8-team fixture of tests/standings.test.js with today = 2026-10-23, a game day. At tip-off the 5 starters of team 0 are in running with points 1, day '2026-10-23'.
   - leagueRace total and P(1st) before: 1024.4 / 12.5% for every team.
   - At tip-off: team 0 shows 944.0 / 2.3% and every other team 1024.4 / about 14%. The total fell by 80.4 = 5 x (17.08 expected - 1 scored), against sd 86.
   - One player's season expectation: 102.44 before, then 1 + 85.37 = 86.37 at tip-off.
3) race82.mjs is the same setup with an 80-game calendar (sd 979). Team 0 falls 13658.5 -> 13578.2 and P(1st) 12.5% -> 11.1%, while the other teams rise to about 12.8%. All of this comes back only when the game becomes final and leaves running.
verdict.fix:
Keep the not-yet-played part of a running game in the expectation instead of dropping the game.

1. Measure how much of the game is gone. In fetchLiveGames/eventInfo (src/live.js), carry the game's elapsed share from ESPN's status: elapsed = min(1, ((period-1)*12 + 12 - clockMinutes)/48). Overtime counts as 1. livePoints puts it on the running entry as {points, day, elapsed}.
2. Count the rest of the game. In expectedPoints (src/season.js:248), stop filtering out `g.date===running`. Count that game with weight p = max(0, 1 - elapsed). Use the per-game value, without the injury factor or the availability share, because the player is already on the floor. This adds value x (1 - elapsed) to points and the same share to games, or keep the games column without it, since games left should not include a game in progress.
3. Keep the old drop where it belongs. Transfer gains must still ignore a running game. Either keep the drop when ctx.now / a gains flag is set, or apply the remainder only in leagueRace and ahead(): rest += value x (1 - elapsed) for each running player.
4. Update ACCEPTANCE.md:136 and the test at season.test.js:235. They should assert "running points + expected remainder", not "game not expected".

A cruder interim fix: use max(0, 1 - running.minutes / forecast.minutes) as the remaining share.

findings.title: seasonEnding zeroes an Out player's season when his comment mentions a past season-ending injury, and misses 'rest of the regular season'
findings.claim: '\bseason[- ]ending\b' matches anywhere in the comment. PAST strips only the exact phrase "last season's season-ending". A routine one-game Out note that recalls last season's surgery therefore sets injuryFactor to 0 for every remaining game. The regex also requires 'season' right after 'the', so 'miss the rest/remainder of the (2026-27) regular season', the usual phrasing of late-season shutdowns, is not recognised.
findings.reproduction: Scratch file review2/season/rx.mjs, status Out/OUT. 'Smith (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game as he continues to work back from the season-ending surgery he underwent in March.' -> true, so 0 games for the season. 'Jones (Achilles) will not play Friday, … since returning from a season-ending Achilles tear suffered in 2025.' -> true. 'Brown is expected to miss the rest of the regular season…' -> false. 'Brown will miss the remainder of the 2026-27 regular season.' -> false.
findings.fix: Require a forward-looking context for 'season-ending' (for example 'suffered/sustained/has a season-ending … (on|this|Monday…)' and not followed by 'in <month/year>'), or apply it only when returnDate falls after the regular season. Allow an optional 'regular ' before 'season' in the miss/rest/remainder patterns. Add the cases above as tests.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. The defect is reachable through the shipped code. In this branch, src/season.js:210 adds `\bseason[- ]ending\b` to OVER with no context. The only guard is PAST (line 211), which strips just the literal phrase "(last|previous|past|20xx-yy) season's season-ending". In the same branch, injuryFactor changed from `back&&day>=back?1:0` to `return 0` for any seasonEnding report. So a false match now removes every remaining game, whatever ESPN's return date says. On origin/main the regex had no 'season-ending' alternative, and a return date still restored the games after it. The false positive is therefore a regression this branch introduced, and it costs more than before.

The false negative is older: main's regex also missed 'rest of the regular season'. The new OVER claims to cover 'rest/remainder of the season' but still requires 'season' straight after 'the ' (or after the 2026-27 tag), so 'regular season' never matches.

Other paths that use the same predicate:
- the expectedPoints week/month/season horizons, via injuryFactor;
- playRate, through the `out` guard;
- the market alerts / injured-target filter at season.js:505.

So one bad match zeroes the player's season value everywhere: advice, the standings outlook and the alerts.

What limits severity: none of the 90 entries in the deployed ESPN feed (public/data/sports-current.json, parsed with parseInjuries) is misclassified. Today only Veesaar, Oweh and Simmons (all OFS), plus Furphy and Hukporti, are flagged, and all five are genuinely season-ending. No other captured feed in the scratchpad contains a past-tense 'season-ending' or a 'regular season' shutdown comment. The defect is latent for the current data and will bite whenever ESPN or RotoWire writes such a note for an Out player. That makes it medium, not high.

Side note, not part of this finding: scripts/projection_model.py:819 ENDING still uses main's old regex, while its docstring says it reads entries 'as src/season.js injuryFactor reads it'. | Comment | seasonEnding | Season games / FP |
|---|---|---|
| "Smith (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game as he continues to work back from the season-ending surgery he underwent in March." | true | 0.0 / 0 |
| "Smith (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game." (same report, comment shortened) | false | 69.1 / 2074 |
| "Murray (knee), who missed the remainder of the season last year with a torn ACL, will not play Thursday." | true | 0 |

findings.title: transfersThisWeek counts the free pre-season deals, so record() warns of 9 transfers in week 1

findings.claim: transfersThisWeek does not exclude rules.js isFreeTransfer deals, so the 20.10 pre-season moves count against tour 1. record() takes max(transfersThisWeek, fblTransfers.used). transfersLeft and the notifier use it whenever Sports.ru's counter is missing. findings.title: An ESPN line with MIN '0' switches perGame to the old 10-game shrink for the player's whole season
findings.location: src/season.js:132 (minutes.some(m=>!(m>0)) fallback) together with withBoxScores at src/season.js:679-680
findings.claim: A final ESPN line for a few-seconds appearance (MIN '0', Sports.ru row still 00:00) becomes played:true with minutes '0'. perGame then abandons the calibrated estimator for all of the player's games. inseason_calibration.py never sees such games (played() needs min>0), so JS no longer mirrors Python.

findings.fix: In perGame, skip the minute model only for games without minutes (or exclude 0-minute rows from the rate and minutes sums), not for the whole set.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this myself; the defect is real. Two notes on scope: it is short-lived, and it already exists on origin/main, so the audit branch did not introduce it.

How it happens:
- liveGamePoints keeps any ESPN line that has stats. A MIN '0' line becomes {minutes:0, counting:points-1}. boxScorePoints even says so on purpose ("+1 even with zero minutes shown"), and tests/season.test.js:146 checks it.
- withBoxScores (src/season.js:679-680) writes that line over a final game. If Sports.ru has not listed the row yet, or still shows it as '00:00' (parse_games treats '00:00' as played:false), `exact` falls back to x.minutes=0. The row becomes {minutes:'0', played:true}.
- perGame (src/season.js:132) has a check meant for rows with no minutes: `minutes.some(m=>!(m>0))`. It also fires on a real 0. So the calibrated per-minute estimator is dropped for every game of that player's season, and the plain (10*prior+sum)/(10+n) shrink is used instead.

Why this is wrong:
- A Sports.ru row for the same cameo, with exact seconds like '00:04', goes through the calibrated estimator normally. So the same appearance gives very different numbers depending on how it is written.
- Python's played() is g['min']>0 on decimal minutes. It keeps sub-minute appearances and only drops true zeros, so it never switches estimator for the whole season.

How far it reaches:
- withBoxScores runs only in the browser (season-ui.js scoreBoxes), on ESPN's yesterday/today games.
- The wrong value lasts from the final whistle until Sports.ru lists the exact minutes, or until the game leaves the ESPN window.
- It only hits players with an appearance under about 30 seconds.
- While it lasts, every perGame user sees the changed value for that player: playerOutlook, transfer options, expected points and the standings simulation.
- On origin/main the same two lines exist: the fallback at old line 84, and String(x.minutes) at old line 464.

Low severity fits: wrong advice numbers for one player for a few hours, in a rare situation.

- Setup: 8 Sports.ru games with exact minutes ('14:12', '18:40', ...; 9, 14, 6, ... FP), then a 2026-11-08 row of {minutes:'00:00', played:false}.
- Before the cameo: perGame = 9.367, with the minutes estimate at 18.15.
- The real ESPN path: liveGamePoints on a box line with MIN '0' and REB '1' gives {points:2, minutes:0, counting:1}. withBoxScores with a final event at 2026-11-08T00:30Z turns the row into {minutes:'0', points:2, played:true, source:'ESPN'}.
- After the cameo: perGame = 9.977, and `minutes` is undefined. That equals the plain shrink (10*prior+sum)/(10+9) = 9.977 exactly.
- The same cameo as a Sports.ru row '00:04' gives 8.166. A '0:01' row gives 8.190.
- So the ESPN '0' line puts this player about 1.8 FP/game above what the calibrated estimator gives for the same appearance, and +0.61 above his pre-cameo value.
- The case with no Sports.ru row at all goes the same way: the row gets minutes '0', and the value is 9.977.

verdict.fix:
Fix it in perGame (src/season.js:132): fall back only when a played game has no minutes at all, not when its minutes are a real 0. For example:
`const noMin=played.some(g=>String(g.minutes??'').trim()===''); if(!played.length||!(priorMinutes>0)||noMin) return {...out,value:(PRIOR_GAMES*prior+sum)/(PRIOR_GAMES+played.length)};`

With that change, a 0-minute appearance goes through the calibrated estimator as an m=0 game: counting = points-1, and it still adds its participation term. That is how a '00:04' Sports.ru row is already handled, and how Python treats sub-minute appearances.

An alternative fix: drop rows whose clockMinutes is exactly 0 from the minute model's rate, minutes and participation sums, like Python's played(), while keeping the other games in the model. Either way, one zero-minute row must not switch the estimator for the whole season. Add a test: perGame with one {minutes:'0', played:true} row must still return a defined `minutes`, and must match the '0:01' result within rounding.

A US-afternoon game of a tour's first day that is filed under the previous tour's last Moscow date therefore counts toward the new tour. windowFact uses the raw g.date, so once the game is played its points move to the previous tour's window. season-availability's crossGroupNote 3 was not applied.

findings.claim: (1) The card says the game ceiling is the player's own 90th percentile over two seasons 'у новичков — игроков того же уровня'. projection_model.apply uses the peer-level ratios for any player with fewer than 10 logged games in two seasons, veterans included. (2) With ESPN 60 games and knownAbsence gamesLeft 30, the source is espn={games:30, projectedGames:60} and the card reads 'ESPN: … × 30', which is not ESPN's projection.

findings.title: In-season build crashes for a season-ending report entry without a return date
findings.claim: seasonEnding is computed as left<=0, and left counts the club games before the build day. From the second day of the season, an 'ending' entry with no returnDate (OFS without a date, or an Out whose comment matches ENDING) gives until='9999-12-31', so returnDate=None but seasonEnding=False. forecast_basis then runs back[8:10] on None and raises TypeError. projection_model.py aborts and the daily Pages build (cron 02:00 UTC, 'Train, hold out and apply' step) fails. The same entry works on 20.10 only because left is 0 that day. The code itself expects undated ending entries: absence() maps them to '9999-12-31', and the ApplyTests fixture 'Gone Rookie' is OFS with no date. None of the 90 live report entries of 20.10 lacks a date, so the crash needs that input to appear.
findings.reproduction: Synthetic league from tests/test_projection_inputs, club schedule AAA every second day from 2026-10-20, player injuries=[{'status':'Out','fantasyStatus':'OFS'}]. pm.apply with generatedAt='2026-10-20' gives games 0, seasonEnding True. With generatedAt='2026-10-22' it raises TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable at projection_model.py:881. Script: review2/pm-av/inseason_ofs.py.
findings.fix: Decide seasonEnding from the absence itself (kind 'ending', or until after SEASON_DATES[1]), not from left<=0. Guard returnDate None in forecast_basis.

findings.title: Season-ending wording read differently from season.js (Furphy forecast 41.5 games while the season tab says out for the season)
findings.claim: projection-inputs copied main's old JS regex. On this branch season.js now uses a wider OVER regex ('season-ending', 'remainder of the season', 'miss the entire 2026-27 season', a guard against 'opener', PAST stripping, keptOut required). Python's ENDING misses these phrases. Even when a comment does match, Python blocks only until ESPN's placeholder returnDate, while JS gives 0 for the whole season. Live case in the 20.10 report: Johnny Furphy, Out/OUT, returnDate 2027-01-02, comment 'torn right ACL ... will miss the remainder of the season'.
findings.reproduction: pm.absence(Furphy entry) gives ('out','2027-01-02'). In the merged rebuild (review2/pm-av/merged-db.json) Furphy has games 41.5, meanSeason 290 and basis '... пропустит 33 матча клуба (до 02.01)'. season.js seasonEnding(same entry) is true, so injuryFactor is 0. Also, pm.absence({'status':'Out','fantasyStatus':'OUT','returnDate':'2026-12-01','comment':'... suffered a season-ending ruptured Achilles.'}) gives 'out' until 2026-12-01; the same holds for 'miss the entire 2026-27 season' and 'will miss the remainder of the season'.
findings.fix: Port the JS OVER/PAST regexes and the keptOut condition into absence(). An ending entry (OFS or matching comment) should block to the end of the season whatever its placeholder returnDate. Add the Furphy wording to the tests.

findings.title: In-season builds count games before the build day as playable: OFS players get seasonEnding False and growing games
findings.claim: The block runs from max(today, opener). So left=82-blocked includes club games already played, during which the player was out, and the post-return healthy chain is fitted over those past games. For a player out for the season (return date after the season) the forecast becomes positive and grows through the season, and the label says he will miss only part of it. From tomorrow's build this hits Veesaar, Oweh, Hukporti and Simmons. Every dated Out gets extra phantom games equal to his share of the games already missed.
findings.reproduction: Same synthetic setup, injuries=[{'status':'Out','fantasyStatus':'OFS','returnDate':'2027-07-01'}]: build 2026-10-22 gives games 0.73, seasonEnding False, basis 'пропустит 81 матч клуба (до 01.07)'. Build 2026-11-20 gives 11.4 games (left 16), 2027-01-01 gives 26.8 games (left 38), 2027-02-15 gives 42.2 games (left 60). Script: review2/pm-av/inseason_ofs2.py.
findings.fix: Count gamesLeft as the club games from the return (or today, if later) to the season end, i.e. leave out games before today and before the return. For an ending absence set games to 0 for the rest of the season and seasonEnding True.

findings.title: Rookies with a dated Out are counted twice in season.js playRate
findings.claim: Rookies and debutants with no NBA record have no availability dict. For them apply() stores the post-block games (share*left) in sources.model.games, and the unconditional games only in knownAbsence.unconditionalGames. While the player is out, season.js takes the prior from availability.unconditionalGames ?? sources.model.games, so it uses the post-block share and injuryFactor removes the blocked games again. projection-inputs' crossGroupNote named knownAbsence.unconditionalGames for exactly this case; season.js does not read it.
findings.reproduction: Merged rebuild, playRate(player,{games:[]},{injuries:Map(espnId->report entry),today:'2026-10-21'}): Jayden Quaintance (Out to 2026-12-03, 23 games blocked) gets 0.411 against an unconditional/post-return share of 0.571 (-28%). Izaiyah Nelson gets 0.352 against 0.418. Mark Williams (veteran, with availability) correctly gets 0.636. Script: review2/pm-av/playrate.mjs.
findings.fix: In season.js, fall back to f.knownAbsence?.unconditionalGames before sources.model.games. Or write availability.unconditionalGames for rookies too.

findings.title: Season-ending players get a full-season replacement credit and outrank healthy starters on the draft board
findings.claim: A known block adds (blocked-delay) replaced games, so an OFS player's slotSeason is 80 x the position's replacement level (about 1121-1142 FP) with 0 own points. draftValue ranks by slotSeason/82. projection-inputs flagged this for slot-value-math (crossGroupNote f), and the projection-model group's slot fix did not address it. The holdout check behind the credit (actual_replaced(None,n)) covers unforeseen zero-game seasons, not a known absence bought at draft cost (pick, Sports.ru price, a transfer).
findings.reproduction: Merged rebuild, priced players sorted by slotSeason: Ariel Hukporti (OFS, meanSeason 0) has slot 1142, rank 87 of 480, above 392 priced players with positive own points, including Nic Claxton (1139 slot, 1003 own) and Maxime Raynaud (1129, 994 own). Ben Simmons (OFS) is rank 95 at 1121. Donte DiVincenzo (55 own) has 1093.
findings.fix: Rank by own points for season-ending or known-block players, or net the replacement credit against the transfer and price cost. At minimum, leave the known-block games out of the slot credit until slot-value-math validates it.

findings.title: The published construction's holdout bias is -43 FP, but only the unpublished unconditional centre is reported and tested as unbiased
findings.claim: HEALTHY_SHIFT was refitted for zero error on players who played their club's first game, an outcome-selected subset. Production applies it to everyone not on the report: 415 of 443 rostered model players (94%, +5.7 games on average), against 296 of 484 (61%) in the holdout. The holdout's non-starters are already over-predicted by about 11.6 games by the unconditional model. On the same holdout the report's own deployedSeasonBias is -43.2 FP (published construction), while seasonBias +4.1 (unconditional) is the figure quoted as 'centre-bias fixed'. The new test asserts only the unconditional bias and the starters-only bias.
findings.reproduction: Merged report: holdout.seasonBias 4.14, deployedSeasonBias -43.20, gamesBias -0.31, healthyStart.unconditionalBias -6.85 and healthyStartBias -0.67 over 296. Non-starter mean: (-0.31*484 - 6.85*296)/188 = -11.6 games. Merged DB: healthyNow=True for 415 of 443 rostered model players.
findings.fix: Report and gate on deployedSeasonBias, fit the shift on a population that resembles the production rule (e.g. players not out at the start for injury), or keep the shift at or below the old weights until a preseason report archive exists.

findings.title: deployed() mixes 63- and 72-game season lengths for 2019/20 in the holdout range pool
findings.claim: For t=2020, deployed() computes the healthy mean with n=season_length(2020)=63. with_games then builds the chain over season_games(2020)=72 games, and Ranges.raw rescales by 63/72, so the 2020 games scenarios average 12.5% below the centre. This repeats the existing mismatch of the unconditional path. It affects only the holdout pool 2020-2025; the production pool 2021-2026 is unaffected.
findings.reproduction: Code path: forward(fit, range(2020,2026)) calls deployed() for 2020, where season_length(2020)=63 but distribution(L=None) uses season_games(2020)=72.
findings.fix: Pass L=n to with_games/distribution in deployed() and forward().
